physics_goals.quote: The CEBAF large acceptance spectrometer (CLAS) is used to study photo- and electro-induced nuclear and hadronic reactions by providing efficient detection of neutral and charged particles over a good fraction of the full solid angle.
physics_goals.value: Study photo- and electro-induced nuclear and hadronic reactions: nucleon resonance (N*) spectrum, nucleon structure

summary.plain: CLAS (the CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer) was a large particle detector in Hall B at Jefferson Lab that recorded what happens when electron or photon beams strike nuclei, mapping nucleon excitations and the structure of protons and neutrons from 1997 to 2012.
summary.technical: Large-acceptance spectrometer in CEBAF Hall B built around a six-coil toroidal magnet with drift chambers, Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters; ran with electron and photon beams up to 6 GeV from 1997 to 2012 (N* programme, DVCS, GPDs, spin structure) before being replaced by CLAS12.
